package_info.why_malicious: If a malicious package is specified as a build requirement in pyproject.toml or setup.py/setup.cfg, and is only available as a source distribution, it can execute arbitrary code during the build process in an isolated environment. This code execution is not captured in lockfiles, making it difficult to audit or detect, and the environment is deleted after use, covering the attacker's tracks.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time (PEP 517/518 build-system.requires resolution), the package manager resolves and installs all build requirements listed in pyproject.toml, potentially as source distributions, which can execute arbitrary code in an isolated build environment, resulting in arbitrary code execution that is not captured in lockfiles.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Specifying build requirements in pyproject.toml allows the package manager to fetch and execute code from source distributions during the build process. If any of these requirements are malicious, their setup.py or build scripts can execute arbitrary code in an isolated environment without user awareness.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, build requirements are expected to be safe, trusted, and auditable, with their versions pinned and tracked. Here, unpinned or untrusted packages can be introduced, and their code executed without being recorded in lockfiles or standard dependency audits.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages use build requirements to specify compilers or build tools (e.g., cffi, setuptools-rust), but should only use trusted, well-known packages with pinned versions.
key_indicators: pyproject.toml [build-system][requires] referencing unpinned or untrusted packages
Build requirements resolved as source distributions (sdist) instead of wheels
No lockfile or dependency record of build requirements
Execution of setup.py or build scripts from build requirements during isolated build

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time (legacy setuptools build), the setup_requires argument causes setuptools to resolve and install the specified build dependencies, potentially as source distributions, which can execute arbitrary code in the build environment, resulting in untracked code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup_requires allows dependencies to be fetched and executed at build-time, and if a malicious package is specified, its setup.py or build scripts can execute arbitrary code in the build environment without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal setup.py usage expects setup_requires to reference safe, auditable, and pinned packages. Here, untrusted or unpinned packages can be introduced, and their code executed without being tracked in lockfiles or dependency manifests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: setup_requires is used for legitimate build-time dependencies (e.g., packaging, wheel), but should only reference trusted, well-known packages with pinned versions.
key_indicators: setup.py with setup_requires referencing unpinned or untrusted packages
setup.cfg with [options] setup_requires referencing untrusted packages
Build requirements resolved as source distributions (sdist)
No lockfile or dependency record of build requirements
Execution of setup.py or build scripts from build requirements during build

attack_chain.action: User installs a package (e.g., cryptography) from source distribution, triggering build requirements resolution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Build requirements are resolved and installed in an isolated environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious build requirement (source distribution) is installed and its setup.py or equivalent is executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution occurs in the build environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code can perform actions such as exfiltrating secrets, modifying files, or installing persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Build environment is deleted after use, erasing evidence and bypassing lockfile-based audits.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of setup.py or arbitrary code during build-time for build requirements
Network activity or filesystem changes during build isolation phase
Installation of build requirements not present in lockfiles
Resolution and installation of source distributions (sdist) as build requirements
file_indicators: pyproject.toml with [build-system][requires] referencing unpinned or unusual packages
setup.py with setup_requires argument referencing untrusted or unpinned packages
setup.cfg with [options] setup_requires referencing untrusted or unpinned packages
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound connections during build-time from isolated build environments
Resolution and download of source distributions from PyPI or other repositories during build
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of source distributions as build requirements, especially in isolated build environments. Flag any build requirements not present in lockfiles or that are resolved as source distributions. Audit pyproject.toml and setup.py/setup.cfg for unpinned or suspicious build requirements. Monitor for network or filesystem activity during build-time that is not typical for the package being installed. Correlate build-time network activity with the presence of untracked build requirements to identify potential malicious behavior.
